summary: Complete target-level planning pass for the accepted parent’s local-dynamics remainder. The parent’s escape potentials, reduction, multipliers and canonical measures remain the owners of those declarations. This follow-up adds classical and Berkovich Fatou–Julia theory, both support identifications, the complex transfer and entropy proof endpoints, and a publicly sourced refinement of Zieve’s sharp period bound. Analytic and generic entropy suppliers are explicit requests and gaps; complete records a finished planning pass, not implemented mathematics or closed prerequisite chains.

nodes.title: Exceptional points
nodes.statement: For a self-map f of X, backwardOrbit(f,a)={x : ∃n≥0, f^n(x)=a} and exceptionalSet(f)={a : backwardOrbit(f,a) is finite}. The n=0 term contains a. For a surjective finite-fibre rational map of degree ≥2 this agrees with finite grand orbit; finiteness of a single fibre does not define exceptional. On the Berkovich line distinguish the classical exceptional set from the set computed on the full analytic carrier.
proofSteps: Use native Nat.iterate and Set.Finite; expose the union of iterated preimages.
For rational maps, finite backward orbit is mapped onto itself; hence it is a finite union of cycles and includes its forward orbit. This proves equivalence with the source’s grand-orbit convention.
acceptance: Do not remove n=0 or confuse degree with the cardinality of a fibre.

sources.match: Finite grand orbits define exceptional points; the rational-map setting identifies them with finite backward orbits.
Uses finite backward orbit, with a separate pure-inseparable alternative.

nodes.title: Classical Fatou and Julia sets
nodes.statement: On a uniform space X define classicalFatou f={x : ∃open U containing x, UniformEquicontinuousOn (n↦f^n) U}; classicalJulia f is its complement. For P¹(C), use the unique uniformity compatible with the compact sphere topology, equivalently its chordal metric. For P¹(K) nonarchimedean, use the chordal metric topology, not the one-point compactification topology on K. On C the local condition agrees with normality of meromorphic iterates for uniform convergence on compact subsets in the spherical target metric.
hypotheses: The abstract predicate uses only a self-map and a uniform space. Rational-map conclusions assume degree ≥2 and the indicated valued field.
proofSteps: Use the native UniformEquicontinuousOn predicate on the whole neighborhood, rather than EquicontinuousAt at its center.
Shrink to relatively compact neighborhoods on the complex sphere; Arzelà–Ascoli identifies local equicontinuity and spherical normality. The complex-manifold identification is a separate supplier.
acceptance: Euclidean equicontinuity on affine C alone is not the sphere predicate.
A pointwise condition without a neighborhood is rejected.

sources.match: Defines local uniform equicontinuity and explains why normality is an equivalent complex definition but can fail over non-locally-compact fields.
Normality of meromorphic iterates defines the complex regular set.

uses.how: Distinguishes good reduction, inseparability and multiplier behavior in the classical line.
Identifies the support of the transfer-limit measure with the irregular set.

nodes.title: Berkovich Fatou and Julia sets
nodes.statement: For a topological self-map f on X put forwardSaturation(f,U)=⋃_{n≥0} f^n(U). A dynamically stable open set U has infinite complement X orwardSaturation(f,U). The omission Fatou set is the union of such U and the omission Julia set is its complement. On the weak/Gelfand topology of P¹,an_K these are F_Ber and J_Ber. Define on the actual seminorm carrier from TB.0; the strong tree metric and the classical chordal topology are distinct topologies. Do not define stability by omitting only two points or even three points in arbitrary characteristic.
hypotheses: K is complete, algebraically closed and nontrivially nonarchimedean for the Berkovich specialization.
proofSteps: The generic predicates are real-bodied Set predicates over an existing topological carrier.
Apply them to the native projective analytic line and rational-map analytification supplied by TB.0; keep the classical embedding and Gauss point visible.
acceptance: Identity on a finite discrete carrier has empty omission Fatou set although its classical equicontinuity Fatou set is the whole carrier.
Use arbitrary open neighborhoods, not only classical discs.

sources.match: Uses infinitely many omitted points for the Berkovich definition.
Explains the exceptional-set qualification, especially for inseparable maps.

uses.how: The local canonical measure has support the Berkovich Julia set.
Good reduction, blowing up and singleton/perfect dichotomy use dynamically stable neighborhoods.

nodes.title: Classical exceptional-set dichotomy
nodes.statement: Over an algebraically closed field, a degree-d≥2 rational map has either at most two classical exceptional points, or characteristic p>0 and a PGL₂ conjugacy to z↦z^(p^r) for r≥1. In the latter case E is the conjugate of P¹(overline(F_p)) and is countably infinite. In particular E is Borel and countable for every valued field here; in characteristic zero it has at most two points.
hypotheses: Algebraically closed field; the absolute value is irrelevant to classification.
proofSteps: A finite grand orbit is permuted bijectively and each point has a singleton inverse fibre for a suitable iterate, forcing total ramification.
More than two such points forces separable degree one. Normalize three fixed points to 0,1,∞ to identify the map with a Frobenius power.
For Frobenius, finite backward orbit is exactly algebraicity over the finite prime field. The non-Frobenius case has at most two exceptional points.
acceptance: The bound |E|≤2 is never asserted without excluding the pure Frobenius case.

sources.match: Classifies the case with more than two exceptional points.
Separates topological degree from total degree and describes the infinite Frobenius exceptional set.

nodes.title: Classical invariance laws
nodes.statement: For a nonconstant rational map on P¹(C) or P¹(K) with the corresponding chordal uniformity, F and J are open/closed complements, completely invariant: f⁻¹F=f(F)=F and f⁻¹J=f(J)=J. They are unchanged by replacing f with f^m, m≥1, and are transported by PGL₂ conjugacy. These rational-map assertions are not universal laws for arbitrary topological self-maps.
hypotheses: Either the complex sphere case, or the complete algebraically closed nontrivially nonarchimedean chordal case; f is nonconstant in that case.
proofSteps: Openness follows from the local definition. For backward invariance restrict to inverse neighborhoods; for forward invariance use openness of the finite holomorphic/rational map and its local normal form.
For iterate invariance write each exponent as mn+i; the finitely many rational maps f^i have uniform Lipschitz bounds in chordal metrics.
PGL₂ maps and inverses have finite chordal Lipschitz constants, so they transport the local uniform condition.
acceptance: The complex and nonarchimedean cases have separate field assumptions, not simultaneous hypotheses.

sources.match: Proves the nonarchimedean invariance and conjugacy laws together.
Uses the corresponding complex normal-family invariances.

nodes.title: Disc criterion for classical stability
nodes.statement: For a family G of rational functions on P¹(K), local chordal uniform equicontinuity at x is equivalent to the existence of a projective disc D containing x such that, for every g∈G, g(D) lies in one residue class. For the family of iterates, x∈F_I iff some sufficiently small disc has this property. Equivalently there is a disc whose forward saturation omits an infinite set of classical points.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: Normalize a target residue class; a rational function omitting the Gauss boundary has a bounded analytic expansion on the disc. The ultrametric coefficient bound gives a common Lipschitz constant after shrinking.
Conversely a common small chordal image bound puts each image into the residue class of its center.

For iterates use the backward-invariant omitted set: either it contains a nonexceptional point, giving infinitely many omitted preimages, or the residue-disc description produces a whole omitted disc.
acceptance: Disc images and coefficient estimates use nonarchimedean analysis; do not import complex Montel for this proof.

sources.match: Relates equicontinuity, residue-disc images and infinite omitted sets.

nodes.title: Periodic points and multipliers
nodes.statement: A classical periodic point a of f over K is in J_I iff its cycle multiplier λ satisfies |λ|>1; it is in F_I iff |λ|≤1. This includes indifferent points. Through the type-I embedding the same alternatives locate a in J_Ber or F_Ber.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: Replace f by the return iterate and move a to 0. If |λ|≤1 choose a small invariant disc using the convergent local expansion. Iterates are uniformly Lipschitz there.
If |λ|>1, every punctured sufficiently small disc is eventually expanded outside itself; take initial points arbitrarily close to a to contradict local uniform equicontinuity.
The Berkovich statement uses the classical-trace comparison, not a multiplier definition on nonclassical points.
acceptance: Over C an indifferent periodic point need not be Fatou; this endpoint is restricted to the nonarchimedean field.

sources.match: Proves both alternatives by invariant and expanding discs.

nodes.title: Empty classical Julia set at good reduction
nodes.statement: If f has good reduction over K, F_I=P¹(K) and J_I=∅. The same holds for potentially good reduction after PGL₂ transport.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
Good reduction or potentially good reduction, respectively.
proofSteps: Good reduction preserves chordal distances up to a factor ≤1; all iterates still have good reduction. Hence the entire family is uniformly equicontinuous on P¹(K).
Use classical conjugacy invariance for potential good reduction.
acceptance: The Berkovich Julia set of the same map is a singleton, not empty.

sources.match: All iterates of a good-reduction map are chordal nonexpanding.

nodes.title: Inseparable maps have empty classical Julia set
nodes.statement: If char K=p>0 and f∈K(z^p) is inseparable, all classical periodic multipliers vanish and J_I=∅. This does not assert potential good reduction or a singleton Berkovich Julia set for every inseparable map.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
Positive characteristic and inseparability, not merely residue characteristic p.
proofSteps: Write f=ψ∘(z↦z^p); ψ has a finite chordal Lipschitz constant C.
Chordal distance under Frobenius is its p-th power. On a disc of radius at most C^(-1/(p−1)), f contracts or preserves each distance; this property persists under iteration.
The chain rule gives multiplier zero for every periodic cycle.
acceptance: This is not a residue-characteristic-zero theorem or a converse to good reduction.

sources.match: Explains the local contraction of inseparable maps and empty type-I Julia set.

nodes.title: Berkovich invariance laws
nodes.statement: On P¹,an_K the Fatou/Julia sets are open/closed complements and are completely invariant under f; F(f^m)=F(f), J(f^m)=J(f) for m≥1; PGL₂ conjugacy transports them. Every classical exceptional point is in F_Ber.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: Images of open sets are open for the finite rational analytic map; finite fibres preserve infinitude when pulling back an omitted set. This proves forward and backward stability.
Group iterates into finitely many residue classes modulo m; infinite omitted complement for f^m yields a stable smaller neighborhood for f using finite fibres.
Homeomorphism transport is formal. Classical exceptional cycles are totally ramified and superattracting, giving stable classical discs and then stable Berkovich discs.
acceptance: Do not put type-II finite-grand-orbit points into the classical exceptional set.

sources.match: Records invariance and exclusion of classical exceptional points; carrier in 6.15(a) is corrected to the analytic line.

nodes.title: Classical trace of Berkovich stability
nodes.statement: If ι:P¹(K)→P¹,an_K is the type-I embedding, ι⁻¹(F_Ber)=F_I and ι⁻¹(J_Ber)=J_I. This compares subsets through the native type-I embedding, whose subspace topology agrees with the classical chordal topology. The full analytic line also contains nonclassical points and is not OnePoint K.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: For x∈F_I choose a disc with infinitely many omitted classical points. Its Berkovich disc has the same images on type-I points, so remains stable.
For a type-I point in F_Ber shrink its stable weak-open neighborhood to a Berkovich disc. Select two omitted points and a separating type-II point.
An image disc containing that separator would contain one omitted point; hence all image discs stay in residue classes at the separator. The disc criterion gives x∈F_I.
acceptance: The analytic carrier is essential; no compactification of the classical point set is substituted.

sources.match: Proves the set-theoretic trace comparison using image discs and a type-II separator.

nodes.title: Nonclassical finite grand orbits
nodes.statement: If a point ζ of type II, III or IV has finite grand orbit under f on P¹,an_K, there is exactly one nonclassical point with this property; it is type II, fixed and totally invariant. Moving ζ to ζ_G by any PGL₂ transformation makes f have good reduction.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: Pass to an iterate fixing all points in the finite orbit; the inverse fibre of each is a singleton and the local degree equals the full degree.
Two such points would bound an annulus whose logarithmic modulus is multiplied by d^n under the iterate. Fixed endpoints force its positive modulus to equal d^n times itself, a contradiction.

The full-degree local branch excludes type III/IV; normalize the unique type-II point to Gauss. Every residue component maps into one component, so zeros and poles cannot share a component; the resultant is a unit.
acceptance: The needed exact annulus-stretching and point-type assertions are in the TB.1 request; a reference to an unread Fatou-component classification is not a substitute.

sources.match: Uses full-degree annulus stretching and the zero/pole criterion for good reduction.
Records the same nonclassical exceptional-point rigidity.

nodes.title: Gauss Julia set at good reduction
nodes.statement: For a degree-d≥2 good-reduction map over K, J_Ber={ζ_G}. Every point outside ζ_G lies in F_Ber. If f has potentially good reduction, the Julia set is the transported type-II point.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
Good reduction, with the potential-good-reduction conclusion obtained by conjugacy.
proofSteps: A residue component either has a periodic forward itinerary, omitting all other components, or has a wandering itinerary, omitting a predecessor component. Thus every point outside Gauss has a stable neighborhood.

Prove Gauss is Julia directly: a weak-open neighborhood contains all but finitely many residue components. Any components omitted by all its forward images form a finite backward-invariant residue set.

After an iterate each omitted residue direction is fixed with full local degree; forward images of the neighborhood’s thin annulus fill that component except at most one classical point. The omitted complement is therefore finite, even for pure Frobenius.
Transport under PGL₂. This direct proof does not depend on Julia nonemptiness from Fatou-component classification.
acceptance: For z^(p^r) the infinite classical exceptional set does not make Gauss Fatou.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.19, p.65; Proposition 6.23, p.68
sources.match: The Gauss-neighborhood annulus argument and residue-component proof give the singleton without invoking Theorem 6.21.

nodes.title: Nonarchimedean preimage equidistribution
nodes.statement: Let μ_f be the parent canonical Radon probability on P¹,an_K, and E the classical exceptional set. For every Radon probability ρ with ρ(E)=0, d^(-n)(f^n)*ρ converges weakly to μ_f. Conversely, convergence implies ρ(E)=0. Pullbacks count analytic local degrees, including inseparable multiplicity. In particular normalized preimages of any a outside E converge, and μ_f is the unique balanced probability assigning E mass zero.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: Identify the parent Δg_F+δ_G measure with the telescoping pullback construction of FRL Proposition-Definition 3.1: their potential difference is constant by uniqueness.
Represent ρ−δ_G=Δu with u≤0, possibly singular. Prove d^(-n)u∘f^n→0 on the hyperbolic line, then use Hartogs and weak Laplacian convergence.

Near exceptional attracting cycles use ρ’s arbitrarily small mass in small discs. Outside those basins and for separable degree >1, pass to an iterate and use diam(fζ)≥C diam(ζ)^(d−1); the resulting (d−1)^n growth is dominated by d^n.

For separable degree one normalize to a Frobenius power. The residue orbit is periodic or wanders through disjoint classes; in the latter case their ρ-masses tend to zero. This handles the infinite exceptional set without an at-most-two assertion.

Any positive ρ-mass on the countable classical E gives positive mass to a finite exceptional cycle. Its periodic atomic pullback part cannot converge to the parent measure, which has no type-I atoms. For balanced exceptional-null ρ, convergence of its constant normalized-pullback sequence proves uniqueness.
acceptance: No claim of atom-freeness at all Berkovich points: a Gauss atom is allowed.
The requested TB.1 Hartogs theorem must permit singular potentials, not only bounded continuous ones.

sources.locator: Proposition-Definition 3.1 and equations (3.1)–(3.2), pp.20–21; Theorem A and its proof in §3.2, pp.22–25
sources.match: Constructs the same balanced measure and proves convergence through the exceptional-basin, diameter-growth and Frobenius cases.

nodes.title: Canonical support lies in the Berkovich Julia set
nodes.statement: For the parent μ_f, supp μ_f⊆J_Ber and J_Ber is nonempty. This holds in arbitrary characteristic and does not assume countable metrizability of P¹,an_K.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: When separable degree >1, a stable open U has an infinite omitted set A, so some a∈A is outside the finite classical E. Each normalized pullback δ_a assigns U mass zero.

Use preimage convergence and the open-set inequality μ_f(U)≤liminf μ_n(U)=0. Equivalently test compactly supported continuous nonnegative functions in U; this version works on general compact Hausdorff spaces. Native support membership excludes U.
In the pure Frobenius case conjugate to good reduction; the parent measure is Dirac at the transported Gauss point and the direct Gauss Julia theorem supplies containment.
Radon inner regularity makes support conull; probability mass one implies nonempty support. Thus Julia is nonempty without importing the Fatou-component classification in Benedetto Theorem 6.21.
acceptance: Atomlessness does not imply that E is disjoint from the support; the argument uses a null open neighborhood instead.

sources.locator: Theorem A, pp.2–4; support discussion at start of §3.2, p.22
sources.match: States Julia support; here its support-containment step is derived from the proved convergence to avoid a classification dependency.

sources.locator: Definition 6.14, p.63; proof of Theorem 6.19, p.65
sources.match: The omission definition and direct Gauss argument handle the two cases.

nodes.title: Berkovich blowing up and minimality
nodes.statement: If an open U meets J_Ber, ⋃_{n≥0}f^n(U) contains P¹,an_K\E, with E the classical exceptional set. Consequently J_Ber is contained in every closed backward-invariant S with S\E nonempty; the Julia set is the smallest nonempty closed completely invariant set not contained in E. If J_Ber has at least two points, it has no isolated point.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: If U meets J, its forward saturation has finite complement A by the definition. Since A is backward invariant, every point of A has finite grand orbit.
Classical points in A belong to E. A nonclassical point in A forces potential good reduction by finite-grand-orbit rigidity. The singleton Julia point would then lie in U, contradicting its omission.
For a∈S\E every U meeting J contains a backward iterate of a. Closedness and backward invariance imply J⊆S.

If a Julia point were isolated, apply blowing up to a neighborhood meeting J only there. Complete invariance then forces its backward orbit to be finite, and the nonclassical rigidity forces a singleton Julia set.
acceptance: Use S\E≠∅, not merely |S|≥3, in the inseparable case.

sources.match: The shared blowing-up argument gives minimality and the no-isolated-point alternative.

nodes.title: Berkovich canonical measure has Julia support
nodes.statement: For every f of degree ≥2 over K, the native measure support of the parent canonical measure is exactly J_Ber: supp μ_f=J_Ber. The support is nonempty and compact, f⁻¹(supp μ_f)=supp μ_f=f(supp μ_f), and μ_f gives the classical exceptional set mass zero.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: The previous containment theorem gives supp μ⊆J and nonempty support.

Local-degree measure pullback has support f⁻¹(supp μ); balance f*μ=dμ gives backward invariance of support. Closedness comes from the native support theorem; compactness follows from the native compact analytic carrier.
The parent canonical-measure-is-probability theorem gives no type-I atoms; E is countable, so μ(E)=0. Conull support then has a point outside E.
Apply Julia minimality to S=supp μ for the reverse containment. Pushforward invariance and surjectivity give the image equality.
acceptance: Good reduction yields a type-II Dirac mass, compatible with no type-I atoms.

sources.match: Uses equality of canonical-measure support and the Berkovich Julia set.
Identifies the equilibrium measure support with Julia.

nodes.title: Singleton and perfect Julia sets
nodes.statement: The following are equivalent: J_Ber is a singleton; J_Ber is at most countable; J_Ber has an isolated point; f has potentially good reduction. In that case the point is type II and μ_f is its Dirac mass. Otherwise J_Ber is nonempty, uncountable and perfect.
hypotheses: K complete and algebraically closed with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value; f∈K(z), degree d≥2; arbitrary characteristic unless restricted.
proofSteps: Potential good reduction gives the transported Gauss singleton. A countable nonempty compact Hausdorff space has an isolated point by the Baire theorem: without isolated points it would be a countable union of nowhere-dense singletons.

An isolated Julia point forces a singleton by blowing up. Complete invariance then gives a nonclassical finite grand orbit, since classical exceptional points are Fatou; rigidity gives potential good reduction.
Alternatively singleton support of a Radon probability is Dirac, and the parent point-mass criterion gives the same converse.
acceptance: Perfect means closed with no isolated points in the weak topology; no second-countability assumption is introduced.

sources.match: Connects countability, isolated points, singleton Julia and potential good reduction.

nodes.title: Complex blowing up and inverse branches
nodes.statement: For f on P¹(C), J is nonempty, perfect and completely invariant; E has at most two points and lies in F. For every open U meeting J and every compact K⊆P¹(C)\E, there exists N with K⊆f^n(U) for all n≥N. The backward orbit of each a outside E is dense in J. On a disc avoiding critical values, each inverse branch is holomorphic and branches with disjoint images form a spherical normal family; branches approaching J shrink on smaller compact discs.
hypotheses: f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.
proofSteps: Import meromorphic Montel for three omitted target values. An open U meeting J cannot have all forward images omitting three distinct values; exceptional classification isolates the permanent omissions.
Use finite holomorphic local degree and critical values to form inverse branches on discs. Their disjoint images omit common values, hence are normal.

A nonconstant subsequential inverse-branch limit would give an open image with bounded forward iterates and thus a Fatou neighborhood; this contradicts approach to J. Compactness upgrades the shrinking and covering statements.
Nonemptiness follows because globally normal iterates on the compact sphere would have uniformly bounded degree under local normal convergence, while deg(f^n)=d^n. Backward density gives perfection.
acceptance: The ConformalMapping L1 bounded holomorphic-family theorem alone is not meromorphic Montel with three omitted sphere values.

sources.match: Supplies uniform compact blowing up, normal inverse branches and the inverse-branch counting estimates.

nodes.title: Lyubich transfer limit
nodes.statement: For f on P¹(C) define the native continuous-function operator Aψ(z)=d⁻¹∑_{f(w)=z}deg_w(f)ψ(w). There is a Radon probability ν_f such that A^nψ converges to the constant ∫ψ dν_f uniformly on every compact subset of P¹(C)\E. It is atom-free and balanced and supp ν_f=J. In particular d⁻n(f^n)*δ_a converges weakly to ν_f for a outside E. No new transfer-operator carrier is required; use continuous linear maps on native continuous functions.
hypotheses: f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.
proofSteps: Finite local-degree branches make Aψ continuous even across critical values and give ||A||≤1, positivity and A1=1.

First use a compact L⊆P¹(C)∖E with f⁻¹L⊆L. Inverse-branch counting and normality prove equicontinuity of A_L^nψ. At critical preimages use continuous roots; at a nonexceptional period-r point the return multiplicity t<d^r makes the unresolved branch weight (t/d^r)^k tend to zero. Arzelà–Ascoli gives relatively compact orbits in C(L).

Use the almost-periodic Banach contraction splitting of Lyubich §2. Peripheral eigenfunctions must be constant and eigenvalue 1: a modulus maximizer and backward-density force equality on J. The transient part tends to zero.

The exceptional cycles have forward-invariant neighborhood bases. Every compact K outside E lies in such a compact backward-invariant L. Julia is contained in each L by backward density. The measures constructed on different L agree by evaluating the same transfer limit at a fixed Julia point, so uniform convergence descends to K.

The resulting positive normalized functional is represented by a Radon probability using Riesz–Markov. Duality gives balance and preimage convergence. On Fatou neighborhoods the inverse-branch estimates give zero mass; backward-density gives positive mass to every neighborhood meeting J.
A positive maximal atom of a balanced probability forces a finite backward orbit; those points lie in E, outside J. Thus the Julia-supported measure is atom-free.
acceptance: The generic Banach splitting and Radon functional representation are explicit supplier contracts, not hidden in the term convergence.

sources.locator: Theorem 1 with Lemmas 1–2, pp.358–362; Theorem 2, pp.362–364; §2, pp.352–354
sources.match: Proves the transfer limit, support and normalized preimage convergence via almost-periodic splitting.

nodes.title: Complex canonical measure comparison and support
nodes.statement: The parent archimedean measure μ_{f,∞}=Δg_F+ω equals ν_f from the complex transfer limit. Hence its native support is the classical Julia set, and it is the unique atom-free balanced Radon probability. More generally it is the unique balanced Radon probability with zero mass on E, and every nonexceptional point has normalized preimages converging to μ_{f,∞}.
hypotheses: f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.
The sphere measure-valued Laplacian supplier must first construct the parent measure and establish its positivity, mass one, atomlessness and balance.
proofSteps: The parent measure is atom-free, hence μ(E)=0 because E is finite. For each continuous ψ, balance says ∫A^nψ dμ=∫ψ dμ.
Transfer convergence holds at every point outside E and |A^nψ|≤||ψ||; dominated convergence identifies ∫ψdμ with ∫ψdν. Equality of Radon measures on continuous tests proves μ=ν.
The same reasoning proves uniqueness for every exceptional-null balanced probability. Support equality and preimage convergence now transport through the equality.
acceptance: This is a refinement supplying the parent endpoints, not a second canonical-measure construction.

sources.match: Lists the atom-free balanced measure and preimage characterization.
The transfer limit identifies the balanced exceptional-null measure.
Uses the complex canonical measure and Julia support.

nodes.title: Degree and topological entropy
nodes.statement: For the sphere map f, Mathlib’s native topological entropy Dynamics.coverEntropy f P¹(C) equals the EReal image of log d.
hypotheses: f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.
proofSteps: Use the spherical Bowen metric max_{0≤j<n}Δ(f^j x,f^j y). Inverse-branch counting and a finite critical-disc decomposition give the source bound C(ε)n⁵d^n for maximal separated sets.
Take limsup of logarithmic covering counts divided by n; native net/cover entropy comparison gives the upper bound log d.
Uniform conditional weights on generic inverse fibres give h_ν(f)≥log d; the generic measure-to-topological entropy inequality then gives the lower bound.
acceptance: The entropy is for the full compact sphere and the logarithm is natural. A polynomial count factor vanishes after division by n.

sources.match: Bounds separated-set growth by a polynomial factor times d^n; §5, Theorem 4, p.367 supplies the matching measure-entropy lower bound.

nodes.title: Entropy of the canonical measure
nodes.statement: The invariant probability ν_f=μ_{f,∞} has Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy h_{ν_f}(f)=log d. The Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy carrier and partition API belong to the generic ergodic supplier; this packet does not define a competing entropy.
hypotheses: f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.
proofSteps: Pushforward invariance follows by duality from balance. Critical points have zero mass since ν is atom-free.
Disintegrate ν over the inverse fibres; almost every fibre has d distinct noncritical points, each conditional weight 1/d. The fibre entropy is log d.
Use the generic conditional-entropy formula to obtain hν(f)≥log d; combine with the measure-to-topological entropy inequality and the native topological entropy result to obtain equality.
acceptance: Balance alone is not a definition of maximal entropy; the generic entropy formulas must be supplied.

sources.locator: Proposition 5 and Theorem 4, pp.366–367; Theorem 7, pp.375–376
sources.match: Computes fibre weights and entropy, then matches the topological upper bound.

nodes.title: Unique maximal-entropy measure
nodes.statement: If η is any f-invariant Borel probability on P¹(C) with h_η(f)=log d, then η=ν_f=μ_{f,∞}. Thus the parent archimedean maximal-entropy endpoint is supplied by the identification, the entropy value and this uniqueness theorem.
hypotheses: f∈C(z), algebraic degree d≥2, acting holomorphically on the compact Riemann sphere with spherical topology.
Invariant means pushforward invariance, not balance; competitors need not be atom-free.
proofSteps: For a distinct ergodic η, singularity with ν and local inverse branches produce a positive-η set whose preferred inverse-branch blocks occur with frequency above the uniform 1/N threshold.
Apply the existing Birkhoff node to the indicator of this positive-η set. Count branch words with this excessive frequency using binomial estimates/Stirling: their growth rate is θ<N.
The critical-disc Bowen-net construction contributes only a polynomial factor. Lyubich’s positive-measure-set entropy lemma, proved using Shannon–McMillan–Breiman, gives hη(f)<log d.
For general invariant η use the generic ergodic decomposition and entropy integration theorem; almost every ergodic component of a maximizing η must maximize and thus equal ν.
acceptance: A uniqueness proof restricted to balanced measures does not prove this theorem.

sources.locator: §7, Lemma 1 and Theorem 9 with proof, pp.379–384
sources.match: Uses positive-measure Bowen entropy, excess-frequency branch-word counting and ergodic decomposition for uniqueness.

nodes.title: Power-map acceptance across places
nodes.statement: For f(z)=z^d, d≥2, on P¹(C), J is the unit circle and μ is normalized angular probability there; F consists of |z|<1 and |z|>1 including infinity, and E={0,∞}. On P¹(K) the same map has good reduction, J_I=∅, J_Ber={ζ_G}, and μ=δ_{ζ_G}. In characteristic p and d=p^r, the nonarchimedean classical exceptional set is P¹(overline(F_p)), even though the Berkovich Julia set remains the Gauss singleton.
hypotheses: Separate complex and nonarchimedean specializations of the same power map; d≥2.
proofSteps: The parent escape-rate formula is log max(|z|,1). Its complex normalized Laplacian is angular probability on the unit circle; its nonarchimedean Laplacian is Gauss Dirac minus infinity Dirac.
Iterates converge to 0 or infinity off the complex unit circle, while radial perturbations on the circle are eventually separated.
Use good reduction for the nonarchimedean conclusions and exceptional classification for the characteristic-p warning.
acceptance: Test total mass one and Δlog⁺|z|=ω−δ∞ on the sphere; using 2π times angular mass fails.
This imports the existing power-map object; no new power-map definition is introduced.

sources.match: Computes the contrasting classical and Berkovich good-reduction behavior.
Sets the canonical local measure normalization.

nodes.title: Weighted divisibility for p-fold composition
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and H=X+∑b_iX^i be the generic polynomial over Z[b_0,…,b_D]. For 0≤β≤p−1, every monomial c∏b_i^α_i with coefficient c not divisible by p in [X^β](H^p−X) satisfies ∑_{i=0}^{p−1}α_i≥p and 2α_0+α_1≥p−1. Every composition monomial has weight ∑(i−1)α_i=β−1. For β=0 the only monomials with α_0=1 are binom(p,l+1)b_0b_1^l; in particular the term p b_0 is distinguished. Here H^p means p-fold composition, not ordinary multiplication.
hypotheses: Generic finite-degree polynomial; p odd prime.
proofSteps: Track substitution monomials by weighted degree to obtain ∑(i−1)α_i=β−1 and the β=0 binomial exceptions (Lemma 42).
Reduce modulo p; high-index coefficients i≥p cannot occur in the relevant low-degree monomials with α_0
For total low-index degree use the substitution matrix on R[X]/(X^p), with R=F_p[b_0,…,b_{p−1}]/(b_0,…,b_{p−1})^p. The operator is I+N with N^p=0, so its p-th power is I (Lemma 40).
For weighted low degree embed b_0=u b_1² modulo b_1^(p−1), invert b_2, and use nilpotent quadratic preparation to find a root δ in the ideal (b_1) after a monic quadratic extension.

Translate X by δ: substitution becomes triangular with diagonal 1,(1+ε),…,(1+ε)^(p−1), ε^(p−1)=0. The cyclotomic product gives characteristic polynomial t^p−1; Cayley–Hamilton gives the required identity (Lemma 41). The exact preparation step is retained as an algebra supplier gap.
acceptance: Keep p-fold composition distinct from the polynomial power.
This node refines the parent valuation recursion rather than reproducing its bound.

sources.locator: Lemmas 29–30, pp.22–23; Lemmas 39–42 and proofs, pp.28–31
sources.match: The monomial constraints separate p-divisible terms from terms whose coefficient valuation is controlled by low jets.

nodes.title: Sharp p-power jet growth
nodes.statement: Let R be a characteristic-zero DVR of residue characteristic p, v(π)=1 and e_K=v(p)≥1. For H∈R[X] with H(0)∈m and H′(0)≡1 mod m, write c_i(j)=[X^i](H^(p^j)−X), C_i(j)=v(c_i(j)), with v(0)=∞. If p is odd and p^(j−1)≤2e_K/(p−1), then C_0(j),C_1(j)≥(p^j+1)/2 and C_i(j)≥(p^j−1)/2 for 2≤i≤p−1. At the first index ℓ with p^ℓ>2e_K/(p−1), any finite C_0(ℓ) remains finite and then increases by exactly e_K per p-fold iteration. If p=2, C_0(j),C_1(j)≥2^j while 2^(j−1)≤e_K; at the first ℓ with 2^ℓ>e_K a finite C_0(ℓ) likewise grows by exactly e_K. Therefore a point in m of exact H-period p^n, n≥1, satisfies p^(n−1)≤2e_K/(p−1), sharpened to 2^(n−1)≤e_K when p=2.
hypotheses: DVR in mixed characteristic; H is integral and tangent to the identity modulo m; conjugate the selected cycle point to 0.
proofSteps: Odd p: apply weighted coefficient divisibility to bound the next jet by the minimum of p-divisible terms and weighted non-p-divisible monomials. Induct on j as in Proposition 31.

Past the first threshold, every constant-term summand except p c_0 has valuation strictly greater than e_K+C_0; Proposition 32 gives exact noncancelling linear valuation growth and persistence of the other jet bounds.

For p=2 give the short direct argument omitted by the source: if H=X+c_0+c_1X+… then C_0(next)≥min(e_K+C_0,C_0+C_1,2C_0), and C_1(next)≥min(e_K+C_1,2C_1,e_K+C_0,2C_0). The term with i=2 in the derivative carries the factor 2; i≥3 contributes at least 2C_0.
Those inequalities double both lower bounds up to the threshold. Once C_0,C_1>e_K, only 2c_0 can have the least constant-term valuation, so C_0(next)=e_K+C_0 and C_1 stays >e_K.
A periodic 0 eventually has C_0=∞. Finite noncancelling growth past ℓ contradicts that, forcing its period to divide p^ℓ. Translate ℓ into the displayed inequalities.
acceptance: For e_K=1 obtain n=0 for p≥5 and n≤1 for p=2,3.
Zieve Example 35, p.26: 3+(5X−X²)/2 has the cycle (0,3,6) over Z_3; a claimed universally stronger e_K/(p−1) bound for odd p fails.

sources.locator: Propositions 31–32, p.24; Theorem 33, p.25; Theorem 8, pp.8,21
sources.match: Gives the odd-prime induction and sharp bound. The p=2 conclusion is stated with modifications; the displayed two-jet inequalities supply that modification explicitly.

nodes.title: Polynomial realization of a rational cycle
nodes.statement: For a mixed-characteristic DVR R and P,Q∈R[X], let h=P/Q∈Frac(R)(z). Suppose a finite cycle σ lies in R and Q(a) is a unit for every a∈σ. There exists θ∈R[X] with θ(a)=h(a) on σ and with the same reduced return multiplier when the cycle has more than one point in a residue class. For a good-reduction projective rational map, apply this to its residue-return cycle after a PGL₂(R) coordinate change or reciprocal chart. Combining the parent residue-period and multiplier-order factorization with sharp jet growth proves the existing parent Zieve endpoint; it is not a new copy of that endpoint.
hypotheses: Finite K/Q_p for the parent consequence; more generally a DVR and good reduction at every point in the selected projective cycle suffice.
proofSteps: For the finite set S={Q(a):a∈σ} of units, construct a polynomial Ψ with 1−tΨ(t)=∏_{s∈S}(1−t/s). Then θ=P·Ψ(Q) agrees with h on σ.

For two distinct points in one residue class with matching images, the first-order difference quotient shows the derivatives of the corresponding return polynomials agree modulo m. Apply it to θ’s return map and the polynomial realization of h’s return; the derivative of Ψ at a denominator value gives the rational chain-rule derivative modulo m (Lemma 46).

Use the parent reduction of periodic points to pass to the residue-return orbit, all in one residue disc, and normalize it to m. Unit denominators follow from pointwise good reduction; reciprocal coordinates handle a disc at infinity.

The parent period theorem supplies the order r of the reduced multiplier. Replace the return map by its r-th iterate and use the polynomial realization to reach the tangent-to-identity hypotheses of sharp jet growth.
Insert p^(n−1)≤2e_K/(p−1) (and p=2 sharpening) in the parent zieve-period-exponent-bound. No assertion that global polynomial interpolation preserves exact characteristic-zero multipliers is needed.
acceptance: Source access is resolved by the author PDF; the odd-prime coefficient proof still depends on the precisely named preparation gap.
Do not use the unrestricted formal-composition assertion warned against in §2.4, p.32.

sources.locator: Proposition 44 and Lemma 45, p.34; Lemma 46, pp.35–36; Corollaries 48–49, p.37; Theorem 50 and proof, p.38
sources.match: The finite-cycle interpolation and reduced-multiplier comparison transfer the bound to projective rational maps.

gaps.title: Sphere Riesz measures and normalized distributional Laplacian
gaps.detail: Inherited analytic gap, narrowed to an exact supplier contract. On native OnePoint C with its complex charts, construct Δ on differences of subharmonic functions with Radon Riesz measures; Δlog|z|=δ_0 on C, Δlog⁺|z|=ω−δ∞ on the sphere, total mass zero, local positivity, divisor Poincaré–Lelong, weak continuity under locally uniform potential limits, pullback Δ(u∘f)=f*Δu with local-degree multiplicity, harmonic uniqueness modulo constants and continuous-potential atomlessness. Arbitrary continuous functions do not have measure-valued Laplacians: require differences of subharmonic potentials. Current PDE lane C is C² Euclidean potential theory; propose PDE, Part II rather than claiming that lane already supplies these statements. Existing parent nodes remain authoritative until this extension is planned and reviewed.

gaps.title: Spherical meromorphic Montel beyond bounded holomorphic normal families
gaps.detail: Require normality in the compact-open spherical topology for meromorphic maps on a plane domain omitting three fixed distinct sphere values, allowing the constant-infinity limit. Current ConformalMapping L1 covers locally bounded holomorphic families. ConformalMappingPartII:V0 is a value-distribution owner but does not currently state this exact theorem. Route the extension there; identify spherical normality with local uniform equicontinuity using compact-domain Arzelà–Ascoli and the already specified sphere charts, not a new Riemann-sphere construction.

gaps.title: Almost-periodic Banach contraction decomposition
gaps.detail: Lyubich §2, pp.352–354 uses the following generic result, not covered by the current Hilbert self-adjoint OperatorTheory family: a linear contraction with every orbit relatively compact splits into the closed span of unimodular eigenvectors and a subspace whose iterates tend to zero. If only the constant eigenvectors at eigenvalue 1 survive, iterates converge to the corresponding projection. The source proof uses a compact abelian closure of operator powers, Haar averaging and characters. This must be supplied as a Banach/Markov extension of OperatorTheory, Part II; the dynamical inverse-branch and eigenfunction steps are planned here. No Hilbert spectral theorem is cited as supplying it.

gaps.title: Generic measure entropy and maximizing-measure machinery
gaps.detail: PM.4 plans native ergodicity, exactness, conditional expectations and Birkhoff, but not Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. Need finite measurable partition entropy with natural logs and 0log0=0, joins and h(T,P)=lim n⁻¹H(∨_{j<n}T⁻ʲP), hμ(T)=sup_P h(T,P), fibre disintegration and conditional-entropy lower bound, hμ(T)≤Dynamics.coverEntropy T univ, Shannon–McMillan–Breiman and its positive-measure Bowen-set bound (Lyubich §7 Lemma 1), ergodic decomposition and integration of entropy. Propose Probabilistic and metric number theory, Part II; keep the existing PM.4 Birkhoff owner. Until this contract is planned, the Lyubich dynamical entropy proofs are planned but not closed.

gaps.title: Nilpotent quadratic preparation in Zieve’s weighted coefficient proof
gaps.detail: Source access to Zieve’s thesis is resolved. The residual algebra step is precise: in S=F_p[u,b_1,…,b_D,b_2⁻¹]/(b_1^(p−1)), b_0=u b_1², factor g(T)=∑b_iT^i by a monic quadratic T²+b′_1T+b′_0 with b′_1∈(b_1), b′_0∈(b_1²), times a unit formal series. After a monic extension adjoin a root δ∈(b_1). Zieve Lemma 41, pp.29–30 invokes Newton polygons for this preparation over a nilpotent coefficient ring. The current AdicSpaces Weierstrass theorem is over complete valued fields and does not supply this ring statement. A finite nilpotent-ideal lifting proof, with injectivity of the embedding and monic root extension, is needed; it is not claimed as a library baseline fact. This replaces the broad inaccessible-source gap with a localized algebra supplier gap.
